#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Exits 0 when the post-fix test suite FAILS against the pre-fix tree, proving
# the new regression tests are not hollow. Exits 1 if they pass at base.
set -u
root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
base="${1:-f4f8aee}"
work="$(mktemp -d)/base"
git -C "$root" worktree add --quiet --detach "$work" "$base"
cp "$root"/test/*.js "$work/test/"
if (cd "$work" && node --test >"$work/out.txt" 2>&1); then
  echo "FAIL: new tests passed against base $base - they prove nothing"
  status=1
else
  echo "OK: new tests fail against base $base"
  grep -E '^# (pass|fail)' "$work/out.txt" || true
  grep -oE 'not ok [0-9]+ - .*' "$work/out.txt" | sed 's/^/  /' || true
  status=0
fi
git -C "$root" worktree remove --force "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exit $status
EOF

# Audit remediation: order access control, money exactness, and enforceable boundaries

Branch `audit/orders-service-remediation` — `f4f8aee..2a92c69` (3 commits).
Nothing pushed; no pull request opened.

`README.md` §Rules is the authoritative spec for this change. Every defect
below is code contradicting a rule already written there, so no requirement
text changed and `README.md` is not edited. The per-change rationale lives in
the three commit messages; this file compiles the evidence and the gaps.

## Gate result

```
Gate:       FAIL  (1 major finding open, pending one human decision)
Verified:   P1-AC1, P1-AC2, P2-AC1, P3-AC1  (4/4)
Open:       F-P2-2 (major), F-P3-11, F-P3-12, F-P2-5, F-P2-6 (minor)
Merge:      human approval required
```

The gate does not pass, and the one thing blocking it is not code — see
[One decision needed](#one-decision-needed-before-merge).

## What changed

Nine defects, each contradicting a stated rule. `(base)` marks a defect that
predates this branch; `(mine)` marks one this branch introduced and then fixed.

| # | Defect | Rule | Fix |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | Any authenticated customer could read **any** customer's order via `GET /orders/:id` | ownership | Route reads through `getOwned`; the unguarded read left the order service's public surface, so transport cannot reach it again |
| 2 | A `shipped` or `delivered` order could still be cancelled | lifecycle | `TRANSITIONS.shipped` no longer lists `cancelled` |
| 3 | `GET /reports/:name` joined an unvalidated name onto `REPORT_DIR`; an encoded traversal read any file the process could read | exports served from `REPORT_DIR` | Name validated against the generated shape, in a new report **service** |
| 4 | Totals accumulated in binary float — `0.1 × 3` was served as `0.30000000000000004` | totals exact to the cent | All summation runs through integer cents |
| 5 | `totalPages` used `floor`, so the last partial page was unreachable | `totalPages` covers every item | `ceil` |
| 6 | `isAmount` used a fixed `1e-6` tolerance, below double spacing past `~1e8`. It **rejected totals the service itself computed** (an order of `19.99 × 6714245` was created, then could never be paid or shipped) and **accepted `49.000000001`** as payment for a total of `49`, storing it verbatim. `unitPrice: 1e306` overflowed a total to `Infinity` (JSON `null`, CSV `Infinity`) | totals exact to the cent; payment equals total | `isAmount` is exact (`Number(v.toFixed(2)) === v`, safe-cent bound); `fromCents` refuses any total that cannot round-trip, so such an order is a `400` |
| 7 | `gateway.charge()` was neither awaited nor checked: a gateway returning `declined` still marked the order **paid**; an async gateway stored `status: undefined` | payment marks the order paid | Awaited; a non-captured charge is a `409`. A payment is attributed to the **order's owner**, so the owner no longer gets `404` on a payment against their own order |
| 8 | `crypto.scryptSync` ran on the event loop for every unauthenticated `POST /sessions` | — (availability) | Key derivation is async; `createApp` stays synchronous (the admin bootstrap is awaited in `listen()`) |
| 9 | `.gitignore` said `reports/` unanchored, so it also matched `src/reports/`. **The entire reports subsystem was untracked**: a fresh clone could not start (`Cannot find module './reports/routes'`) | — (packaging) | Rule anchored to `/reports/`; file committed |

Also removed: the unused cookie parser, and a single-entry payment-provider
registry that held process-global mutable state (the gateway is now injected).
The user service owns listing and pagination, so transport no longer reaches
into the store. Totals are logged instead of discarded on a `500`.

**Architecture rules now ship as code** in `test/architecture.test.js`,
dependency-free so the zero-dependency promise holds: transport must not
import persistence, transport must not reach `node:fs`, `src/lib/**` imports
nothing internal, currency conversion and formatting live only in
`lib/money.js`, every source file belongs to a declared subsystem, and every
source file is tracked by git. That last rule exists because defect 9 passed
every other rule — they read the working tree, which was fine, while the
committed tree could not boot.

Files: 23 changed, +578 / −84. `src/payments/providers.js` deleted,
`src/reports/service.js` added.

## Evidence

All commands run at `2a92c69` on Node v24.19.0, Windows.

| Command | Exit | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `npm test` | 0 | **50 tests, 50 pass, 0 fail** (20 at base) |
| `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD && node --test` | 0 | 50/50 in a clean checkout — impossible before defect 9 was fixed |
| `bash .alchemy/runs/audit-2026-10-28/tests-fail-at-base.sh f4f8aee` | 0 | **17 named regression tests each fail against the pre-fix tree** |
| `node --test test/architecture.test.js` (mutation matrix, in a copy outside the repo) | 0 | Each of 6 rules fails when its violation is injected; 4 previously-evadable variants (double-quoted `require`, `/ 100`, `node:fs` from transport, `toFixed()`) now caught; no false positive on a comment |
| `node /tmp/e2e/e2e.js` | 0 | `19.99 × 6714245` → `201`, pays `201`, ships `200` (was: unpayable, stuck `pending`). `1e306 × 10` → `400`. CSV reads `134217757.55` |
| `node /tmp/dos/dos.js` | 0 | `GET /users/me` **1.5 ms idle → 2.7 ms** under 20 concurrent logins (was 0.7 ms → 421.5 ms) |
| `node /tmp/probe/probe.js` | 0 | Non-owner order read `404`; cancel a shipped order `409`; `totalPages` 3; total `0.3`; traversal `404` |
| `python .../check_orchestration.py plan …` | 0 | `PASS` — waves `[P1]`, `[P2, P3]`, mode multi-agent |
| `python .../check_orchestration.py gate …` | 1 | `FAIL` — `UNRESOLVED_FINDING: F-P2-2`; criteria 4/4 verified |

Two independent read-only reviewers re-ran their own checks against
`f4f8aee..c7e2b52`:

- **Security review** — 76 adversarial HTTP checks: 4 cross-tenant order and
  payment paths all `404`; 33 crafted report names and raw paths (single and
  double percent-encoding, backslashes, `C:\`, UNC, NUL, trailing dot and
  space, NTFS `::$DATA`, full-width unicode, bare dot segments) with no
  escape from `REPORT_DIR`; 9 token-forgery and expiry variants all `401`.
  Found defects 7 and 8 above, plus the `isAmount` overflow.
- **Correctness review** — found defect 6 and proved my own base-check script
  was passing on a module-load crash (below).

Their findings drove one rework cycle (of a budget of 2): 3 blocking and 6
major findings resolved, each with a test that fails at base.

## What I did not verify

- **`src/reports/` has no pre-fix baseline.** It was never committed before
  this branch, so the traversal fix (defect 3) has no reviewable diff and
  cannot be tested against base. The base-check copies `src/reports/` from
  `HEAD` purely so other tests can load, and makes no claim about reports
  behaviour at base. Its own rule (`no transport file reaches durable storage
  directly`) is therefore excluded from the base-failure list and proven by
  mutation instead.
- **My first base-check was invalid, and a reviewer caught it.** It treated a
  non-zero exit as proof the new tests were not hollow. At base, 5 of 7 test
  files died on the missing reports module and only 6 of 17 tests ran — yet it
  exited 0. It now rejects a load crash and asserts 17 tests by name. One
  earlier test (`an amount one cent off the total is rejected`) turned out to
  pass at base and so proves nothing; it is not in the list.
- **Timing-attack resistance of the token compare is not tested.** The
  constant-time compare has no functionally observable oracle; only
  accept/reject behaviour is asserted. Residual risk, recorded not closed.
- **No concurrency or race testing.** The store is an in-process `Map` and
  capture was synchronous; now that `charge` is awaited, a check-then-act
  window exists between `order.status !== 'pending'` and `markPaid`. Close it
  with concurrent `POST /payments` for one order against a slow gateway.
- **No rate limiting on `POST /sessions`.** Async key derivation removed the
  event-loop stall, not the ability to force unbounded scrypt work. Rate
  limiting is a new capability and out of this scope.
- **Symlink escape from `REPORT_DIR` untested.** It needs filesystem access
  rather than an HTTP request. Close by creating a symlink named
  `orders-<digits>-<hex>.csv` inside `REPORT_DIR` and re-running the download.
- **`APP_SECRET` strength, TLS, and secret management** — only emptiness is
  rejected.
- **Not load-tested, not run against a real payment provider, no migration
  concern** (the store is per-process and in memory).
- **Gate Y (flow optimisation) deliberately not run.** It belongs in the
  iteration after this ships, from a measured baseline: `npm test` wall-clock
  (`ℹ duration_ms`, ~1.1 s for 50 tests) and the one-stage pipeline count.
  Iteration 2 opens on the next cycle after merge, or when the suite passes
  ~10 s. The new base-check adds a git worktree create/remove outside
  `npm test`.

## One decision needed before merge

**May an admin change a customer's order?** Both reviewers independently read
`README.md` §Rules — "Customers read and change only their own orders and
payments. **Admins read all of them**" — as granting admins read but not
write. Today `getOwned` is the single gate for both, so an admin can cancel
and pay a customer's order. The API table lists these routes' caller as
`customer`.

I did **not** change this. It is a requirements question, not a defect: the
answer changes the required behaviour, and silently picking one would bake my
reading of an ambiguous spec into an authorization rule. The data-integrity
half of the finding **is** fixed — a payment is attributed to the order's
owner either way, so the owner can always read a payment against their own
order (`test/payments.test.js` admits `201`, `403`, or `404` and asserts
attribution in the `201` case).

- **If admins may not write**: split `getOwned` into a read gate and an
  owner-only write gate in `src/orders/service.js`, and the test's admitted
  statuses narrow to `403`.
- **If admins may write**: record it in `README.md` §Rules so the next audit
  does not reopen it.

Four minor findings are also left open by choice, each with its reason:
`405` and pre-auth `400` statuses are not in the README's list but are
standard HTTP (`F-P2-5`); the `POST /sessions` timing oracle is already
defeated by the README-mandated `409` on duplicate registration, so closing
only the timing channel buys nothing (`F-P2-6`); `GET /orders?page=99` returns
an empty page rather than `404`, which the README does not forbid; and
`src/reports/` has no pre-fix baseline (`F-P3-12`).

## What I did not verify

- **`src/reports/` has no pre-fix baseline.** It was never committed before
  this branch, so the traversal fix (defect 3) has no reviewable diff and
  cannot be tested against base. The base-check copies `src/reports/` from
  `HEAD` purely so other tests can load, and makes no claim about reports
  behaviour at base. Its own rule (`no transport file reaches durable storage
  directly`) is therefore excluded from the base-failure list and proven by
  mutation instead.
- **My first base-check was invalid, and a reviewer caught it.** It treated a
  non-zero exit as proof the new tests were not hollow. At base, 5 of 7 test
  files died on the missing reports module and only 6 of 17 tests ran — yet it
  exited 0. It now rejects a load crash and asserts 17 tests by name. One
  earlier test (`an amount one cent off the total is rejected`) turned out to
  pass at base and so proves nothing; it is not in the list.
- **Timing-attack resistance of the token compare is not tested.** The
  constant-time compare has no functionally observable oracle; only
  accept/reject behaviour is asserted. Residual risk, recorded not closed.
- **No concurrency or race testing.** The store is an in-process `Map` and
  capture was synchronous; now that `charge` is awaited, a check-then-act
  window exists between `order.status !== 'pending'` and `markPaid`. Close it
  with concurrent `POST /payments` for one order against a slow gateway.
- **No rate limiting on `POST /sessions`.** Async key derivation removed the
  event-loop stall, not the ability to force unbounded scrypt work. Rate
  limiting is a new capability and out of this scope.
- **Symlink escape from `REPORT_DIR` untested.** It needs filesystem access
  rather than an HTTP request. Close by creating a symlink named
  `orders-<digits>-<hex>.csv` inside `REPORT_DIR` and re-running the download.
- **`APP_SECRET` strength, TLS, and secret management** — only emptiness is
  rejected.
- **Not load-tested, not run against a real payment provider, and no
  migration concern** (the store is per-process and in memory).
- **Flow optimisation deliberately not run.** It belongs in the iteration
  after this ships, from a measured baseline: `npm test` wall-clock
  (`duration_ms`, ~1.1 s for 50 tests) and the one-stage pipeline count. That
  iteration opens on the next cycle after merge, or when the suite passes
  ~10 s. The new base-check adds a git worktree create/remove outside
  `npm test`.

## One decision needed before merge

**May an admin change a customer's order?** Both reviewers independently read
`README.md` §Rules — "Customers read and change only their own orders and
payments. **Admins read all of them**" — as granting admins read but not
write. Today `getOwned` is the single gate for both, so an admin can cancel
and pay a customer's order. The API table lists these routes' caller as
`customer`.

I did **not** change this. It is a requirements question, not a defect: the
answer changes the required behaviour, and silently picking one would bake one
reading of an ambiguous spec into an authorization rule. The data-integrity
half of the finding **is** fixed — a payment is attributed to the order's
owner either way, so the owner can always read a payment against their own
order (`test/payments.test.js` admits `201`, `403` or `404` and asserts
attribution in the `201` case).

- **If admins may not write**: split `getOwned` into a read gate and an
  owner-only write gate in `src/orders/service.js`, and the test's admitted
  statuses narrow to `403`.
- **If admins may write**: record it in `README.md` §Rules so the next audit
  does not reopen it.

Four minor findings are also left open by choice, each with its reason: `405`
and pre-auth `400` statuses are not in the README's list but are standard HTTP
(`F-P2-5`); the `POST /sessions` timing oracle is already defeated by the
README-mandated `409` on duplicate registration, so closing only the timing
channel buys nothing (`F-P2-6`); `GET /orders?page=99` returns an empty page
rather than `404`, which the README does not forbid; and `src/reports/` has no
pre-fix baseline (`F-P3-12`).
